task.name: A dirty project root is only detected at landing, after the story's full spend
task.story_text:
## Observed behavior

In adopter run `fe2ccadf2ada` (story `issue-246`, 2026-07-29) a story completed
dev and review, was approved, and then failed at the landing step with:

```
Merge failed: Uncommitted changes in project root: M forge.yaml.
Branch 'feat/issue-246' carries reviewed work. Story is recoverable but unmerged.
```

$5.23 was spent before the refusal, and the reviewed work was left stranded on
`feat/issue-246` with no landing. The modified file in the project root was a
tracked config file that had been modified for the whole run — the blocking
condition was present and detectable before any agent was dispatched.

## Expected behavior

A precondition for landing that is knowable before a run begins should be
evaluated before the run spends, not discovered at the last step. When the state
of the operator's own checkout makes it impossible for a story to land, forge
should surface that at entry and name the offending condition, rather than
paying for dev and review first and refusing afterward. Conditions that can also
arise mid-run should still be caught at the point they can first be observed, so
the operator learns of them while the spend can still be avoided rather than
after it is sunk.

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** an approved story reaches `MERGE_FAILED` with reviewed
  work committed to the feature branch but unmerged, because the project-root
  checkout was dirty.

- **Evidence:** the refusal is raised at
  `src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py:359`, inside `_merge_branch`. Grepping
  `git status --porcelain` across the coordinator shows every other cleanliness
  check targets the *workspace*, not the project root:
  `coordinator/commit_guard.py:93`, `coordinator/review_phase.py:834`,
  `coordinator/dev_phase.py:532`, `coordinator/dev_phase.py:1505`,
  `coordinator/validate_phase.py:853`, `coordinator/completion.py:1446`. No
  sprint-entry or preflight path inspects the project root at all.

- **Ruled out:** not a merge conflict — the merge never began. Not a
  regression of the prior fix for uncommitted operator config leaking into
  unrelated story PRs; that change stopped the leak but did not move the
  detection point earlier.

- **Confirmed cause:** project-root cleanliness is checked only inside
  `_merge_branch`, which runs after dev, review, and approval have completed.

- **Affected code path:** `coordinator/workspace.py` `_merge_branch`; sprint
  entry / preflight, which has no equivalent check.

- **Fix-success criterion:** with a modified tracked file present in the project
  root, a sprint surfaces that condition and names the file before any dev or
  review agent is dispatched, and no story reaches an approved-but-unmerged
  state for this reason.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 addresses the cycle-4 P1: the dependency-resolved pass refused a dirty root in a parallel merge-pr sprint, for an in-manifest parent that never merges into the project-root checkout. Verified the mechanism — completion._finalize_approve gives a merge-pr story landing_status 'pending_integration' with action 'merge-pr', and the scheduler's pending_integration conversion fires only for a story that produced no landing of its own (landing_status is None), so a merge-pr parent is never rewritten to a local merge and lands through its own PR. This is the same carve-out the auto_enabled_dependency_merges warning already makes. Named two derivations once, next to in_manifest_dependency_parents, and drove all three assertion sites from them: config_lands_in_project_root = on_approve == 'merge' or (auto_merge and max_parallel <= 1); dependency_parents_land_in_project_root = max_parallel <= 1 or on_approve != 'merge-pr'. The merge-pr carve-out is parallel-only because sequential mode sets effective_am True for a dependency parent, forcing effective on_approve to 'merge' whatever the configured path says. Sweeping the same 'assume the flag reaches the worker' pattern found it in the auto_merge term too: effective_am is hard-False when max_parallel > 1, so --auto-merge never reaches _finalize_approve there and cannot cause a local merge; the sprint-entry pass no longer refuses on it in parallel mode. The per-story _story_lands_in_root term carried both defects and now shares the same flags, so the worker-side and sprint-side answers cannot diverge. _sprint_lands_locally was left alone — it is already gated on max_parallel <= 1, where dependency parents genuinely do merge locally. Cycles 1-3 (per-story obligation threading, in-manifest filter, two-pass timing) are unchanged and still covered.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A precondition for landing that is knowable before a run begins should be evaluated before the run spends, not discovered at the last step — with a modified tracked file present in the project root, a sprint surfaces that condition and names the file before any dev or review agent is dispatched.
acceptance_criteria.notes: The reported workflow (on_approve merge / --auto-merge in sequential mode) refuses at the sprint-entry pass, before pull_base_branch and the baseline gate (test_run_sprint_dirty_root_aborts_before_pull_and_baseline, test_auto_merge_refuses_in_sequential_mode). The dependency-derived obligation refuses at the dependency-resolved pass, with run_batch_preflight asserted never called. run_task escalates in WORKSPACE with _create_workspace never called.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Conditions that can also arise mid-run should still be caught at the point they can first be observed, so the operator learns of them while the spend can still be avoided.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Each story re-evaluates at its own entry, with the scheduler's per-story obligation threaded through _run_fresh, _run_single_story and _run_inherited_story. test_parallel_dependency_parent_dispatched_with_landing_obligation pins the True case (on_approve none) and test_parallel_merge_pr_parent_dispatched_without_landing_obligation pins the False case.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No story reaches an approved-but-unmerged state for this reason.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Root dirty at entry: the run never starts. Root dirtied mid-sprint: the next story that actually lands refuses at its own entry. Within one story after its entry, landing remains the first observable point and _merge_branch still refuses there, sharing project_root_dirty_status with the entry predicate (test_merge_branch_still_refuses_a_dirty_root).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The refusal must not fire for sprints where nothing merges into the project-root checkout (cycles 2, 3 and 4).
acceptance_criteria.notes: External edges: test_external_satisfied_dependency_does_not_impose_a_landing_obligation. Satisfied in-manifest parents: test_satisfied_in_manifest_parent_imposes_no_landing_obligation. Parallel merge-pr parents: test_parallel_merge_pr_dependency_parent_imposes_no_landing_obligation plus the dispatch-side mirror. --auto-merge in parallel mode: test_auto_merge_in_parallel_mode_imposes_no_landing_obligation. Each is paired with a positive test that fails if the carve-out over-corrects — test_sequential_merge_pr_dependency_parent_still_imposes_a_landing_obligation and test_parallel_pr_dependency_parent_still_imposes_a_landing_obligation, both verified against a forced-False mutation of the flag.

deferred_items: Full suite under this sandbox: 6508 passed, 17 failed — the same environmental failures present since iteration 0 (test_cut_rc_isolation.py 'mkstemp: Operation not permitted'; test_sprint_lock.py PermissionError creating POSIX semaphores). No new failures.

Scope note: the --auto-merge-in-parallel term was not named in the finding. It is the identical 'assume the flag reaches the worker' defect in the same expression, so I fixed it under the pattern-sweep instruction rather than leave a known false positive one line away from the one being fixed.

reviews.summary: The main dirty-root merge precondition is covered, but the sprint dependency pass now falsely aborts parallel merge-pr dependency workflows that do not merge into the project root.

findings.description: In a parallel sprint using on_approve merge-pr, a dirty project root aborts at dependency-resolved when an in-manifest dependency parent is present even though that parent would be landed through merge-pr rather than merged into the project-root checkout.

finding_registry.description: In a parallel sprint using on_approve merge-pr, a dirty project root aborts at dependency-resolved when an in-manifest dependency parent is present even though that parent would be landed through merge-pr rather than merged into the project-root checkout.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
